stories.Headline: South Korea exports extend robust growth on AI-fuelled chip boom
stories.Summary:
South Korea's exports grew strongly in October 2026, driven by an artificial intelligence boom in chips, according to data from the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources released on Sunday, November 1. Working-day adjusted exports rose 76.1 per cent from a year earlier, and the value of shipments reached US$115.3 billion, after a record US$121.1 billion the previous month. On an unadjusted basis, exports rose 93.7 per cent and imports climbed 36 per cent, giving a trade surplus of US$42.5 billion. The figures followed a sharp global sell-off in technology stocks after disappointing earnings and outlooks from major US companies including Amazon.com and Intel.

Semiconductors were the main driver, with chip exports surging 259 per cent to US$56.4 billion. Computer shipments rose 497 per cent, while petroleum products and cars gained 80 per cent and 18 per cent. Exports to China rose about 134 per cent to US$26.98 billion, the fifth straight month above US$20 billion, and shipments to the US rose 186 per cent to US$24.9 billion. Exports to the EU and India climbed 56.4 per cent and 84 per cent. The Chuseok holidays fell in September this year and October last year, which the report said makes working-day adjusted figures a useful gauge.

The continued strength adds to the case for the Bank of Korea to raise interest rates in November, after policymakers stood pat in October to assess increases in July and August. Governor Shin Hyun-song said the export boom puts South Korea on course to exceed US$1 trillion in annual shipments for the first time this year, which the trade ministry said would make it the fourth economy to reach the milestone after the US, China and Germany. Shin said monetary policy will remain restrictive until officials are confident inflation will converge to the bank's 2 per cent target. Consumer prices rose 2.9 per cent in September from a year earlier, and core inflation was 2.8 per cent, both above target.

The economy expanded 1 per cent in the third quarter from the previous three months, beating forecasts of 0.8 per cent, while facility investment jumped 4.1 per cent but private consumption fell 0.2 per cent. The Bank of Korea expects growth this year and next to substantially exceed its August projections of 3.3 per cent and 2.9 per cent. Inflation data due on Tuesday will be another input before the bank's November 26 decision, when it will also release updated growth and inflation forecasts. China and South Korea held the 17th round of negotiations on the second phase of their free trade agreement in Seoul from October 12 to 16, and both sides agreed to accelerate talks toward an early conclusion.

stories.Headline: Opinion | SI is the future of AI – just not in the way Trump thinks
stories.Summary:
US President Donald Trump recently began pushing the use of the term superintelligence, or SI, instead of artificial intelligence in national discourse, according to an opinion article by Xie Ming published by the South China Morning Post on 31 October 2026. Xie Ming is an associate professor at the School of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering at Nanyang Technological University in Singapore. He argues that SI is the right acronym but the wrong meaning, and that it should stand for self-intelligence. He says academics, critics and even major AI companies are calling for a temporary pause in AI development because they have realised the technology's current path is wrong.

Xie Ming writes that producing an intelligent answer is very different from independently acquiring knowledge, deciding what to do and acting appropriately in an unpredictable world. He believes the next great challenge for AI is moving from machine learning towards machine self-intelligence. In a separate report, Politico said Democrats in the US House of Representatives called on Trump to preserve all his requests to AI chatbots and the responses to them. Representatives Jamie Raskin of Maryland and Robert Garcia of California made the demand in a letter, and they want to know whether Grok and other AI systems influenced White House decisions.

The lawmakers asked Trump to keep any requests sent to chatbots including Musk's Grok, OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude during the performance of his duties, along with the AI responses. They also requested a briefing on the matter by 5:00 p.m. on November 11. According to Politico, the request followed reports that Trump had turned to Grok for advice on carrying out some presidential duties, including asking its opinion on how Venezuelans would react to his capture of Nicolás Maduro. The lawmakers said that only a few weeks later Trump ordered the US military, without congressional authorisation, to attack Venezuela and capture President Maduro.

Garcia and Raskin called this example deeply troubling, saying Trump consulted Grok but not Congress about the military deployment, circumventing Congress's constitutional authority to declare war. They said the White House's use of AI chatbots exposes the United States to acute national security risks and to malicious influence by unknown and unaccountable third parties. A White House official said the White House preserves all necessary records in accordance with the law. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the requested briefing.

stories.Headline: Proton CTO manifesto says AI fundamentally changed coding jobs
stories.Summary:
Proton CTO Bart Butler released a three-page manifesto arguing that software engineering jobs have fundamentally changed because of AI, as reported by 404 Media and covered on October 31 and November 2, 2026. The memo says an engineer's role is no longer to write code, and that large language models are not there to help engineers write better code faster. Instead, it says, the job is to help the LLM write better code faster. The memo also says every engineer is now a team leader of models and agents, and that the company must adapt to the state of AI.

The memo drew agreement from several people in tech. Peter Steinberger, an OpenAI employee and creator of the OpenClaw AI agent, said Proton CEO Andy Yen gets it, and predicted that if AI progress over the next two years is even half as fast as the current trajectory, the old software engineer job is gone. David Heinemeier Hansson, creator of Ruby on Rails, wrote that employees upset by the memo are in for a rough ride as the age of agents unfolds. Lauren Tan, a principal engineer at SpaceX, wrote that the time for mourning coding is long over and that every engineer now commands an incredibly elastic and capable workforce.

Proton did not respond to a request for comment from Business Insider, but previously told 404 Media that the company has sometimes been too blunt or too slow in explaining itself to its people. Steinberger said he sympathizes with the loss of identity some engineers feel as AI redefines their jobs, but noted that Butler runs a business and may have limited patience after two years to process, learn, change and grow. Edward Ahn, co-founder of Plover Labs, made a chart of memos from big CEOs about AI, from Shopify to Coinbase to Block, ending with Butler, and said every few months the memo gets a little more honest. The articles do not say what Proton or Butler plans to do next beyond adapting to the state of AI.

stories.Headline: CMA opens Meta investigation over use of publishers’ content for AI
stories.Summary:
The UK's Competition and Markets Authority opened an investigation into Meta's commercial terms for businesses, announcing the case on Friday under the Competition Act 1998. The watchdog will examine whether Meta is abusing a dominant position by imposing exploitative terms on publishers and advertisers. Those terms could let Meta collect content from the websites of businesses and publishers that use its services and use it to build its own products, including AI features, without those businesses having a choice. The CMA acted on concerns from groups including the News Media Association and the Movement for an Open Web, and it said the terms could amount to an unlawful imposition of unfair trading conditions on thousands of UK businesses.

Meta first planned to bring in the new terms on 30 October, then pushed them back to 20 November after talks with the CMA. On 28 October it paused the rollout until it has consulted industry groups, the CMA said. The investigation will first decide whether Meta holds a dominant position in a relevant UK market, and if it does, the CMA will then assess whether the terms abuse that position. No decision has been made on whether Meta broke the law, the regulator said.

Meta said there were no grounds for an investigation, according to Reuters. A Meta spokesperson said the company had already committed not to change its terms without consulting publishers and other stakeholders, and that it welcomed the chance to explain its approach to the CMA. In Norway, a court earlier in the week temporarily banned Meta from enforcing the new terms after 10 media outlets argued they threatened their rights to their content, Agence France-Presse reported. In France, Meta lost an appeal over orders to negotiate with news publishers.

Separately, the CMA is asking Meta for information about Meta One, its business subscription service, after the Federation of Small Businesses raised concerns about small firms posting external links on Facebook and Instagram without paying for a subscription. The CMA has not decided whether to take formal action on that, and it sits outside the new investigation. Meta has not been designated with strategic market status under the UK's new digital markets regime, which gives the CMA wider powers. The CMA board is due to consider its next proposals for that status in spring 2027.

stories.Headline: Investor, Tech Entrepreneur, Mentor, Coach & Thought Leader Dato' Seri Ivan Teh Forecasts the Future of A World of AI
stories.Summary:
Dato' Seri Ivan Teh, an investor, tech entrepreneur, mentor, coach and thought leader, gave his views on the future of artificial intelligence in remarks published by The Manila Times on November 2, 2026, in Kuala Lumpur. The pieces were drawn from an article titled "Genesis of AI" by Yvonne Yoong in Paparazzi, dated October 27, 2026. Teh said every major technology shift has brought disruption and opportunity together, and that AI is no different. He said resistance may feel comfortable for a while, but understanding the change gives people far more control over how they respond.

Teh said businesses stay relevant when they stop asking whether they should use AI and start asking what meaningful problems they can solve better. He prefers to rewrite the saying "If you can't beat them, join them" as: understand it, shape it and make it useful. He said people should embrace transformation without becoming uncritical of it, use AI where it creates value, question it where it creates risks, and always keep the human purpose clear. He described AI as relatively early in its journey, likening humanity to the opening scenes of a movie, and said many organisations are only beginning to move from individual AI tools and experiments toward deeply embedded AI across operations, products and decision-making. He said the larger transformation will come as AI agents, robotics and autonomous systems mature and integrate.

Teh said AI has lowered barriers, so a small business, startup, student or independent creator can now access capabilities that once required enormous teams and resources, but access alone is not advantage. He said winners will be those who know what problem to solve, how to apply the technology meaningfully and how to earn trust. He advocated a "Start Small, Think Big, Scale Fast" approach: begin with a manageable use case, solve a genuine problem, measure the outcome, learn quickly and scale what works. He also called for investing in people, strengthening data capabilities and staying agile enough to rethink processes and business models. He said progress must remain human-centred and responsible, and that society should be ambitious about what technology can do while equally thoughtful about what it should do.

Teh, who is Special Advisor of the Malaysia Retail Chain Association Foundation, said no business succeeds in isolation and that philanthropy is about doing what you can, where you can, when the opportunity arises. He said the foundation brings people together as members of society who recognise they can collectively make a difference, and he hoped it continues to touch lives in practical ways. On leadership, he said ambition has to travel with ethics, trust, security and human-centred thinking, and that leaders should ask whether a technology creates opportunity, empowers people and improves lives. He said leadership is not measured by how quickly one adopts the future but by how responsibly one shapes it, and that the future of AI will be defined as much by judgment as by ingenuity.

stories.Headline: Google, OpenAI, Anthropic pledge new AI scraping controls
stories.Summary:
OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic said they will adopt a new standard that publishers can use to opt out of AI scraping across multiple crawlers. The announcement was reported on October 30, 2026. The standard comes from an Internet Draft that Anthropic's Kevin Kelley submitted to the AI Preferences working group at the IETF on the same date. The IETF's document tracker lists it as an individual draft, which does not represent official IETF standardization activity. Kelley said in a post to the working group's email list that Anthropic has started development to provide the feature.

The draft adds no new directive to robots.txt. A site would write an ordinary rule group under the policy token __usage_ai-training, using Allow and Disallow as usual, and the draft gives an example of opting out of AI training on an entire site except for the /press-kit/ folder. The token's meaning comes from the working group's vocabulary draft, which defines AI Training as using content to modify a generative AI model's learned parameters, and models that only do non-generative tasks like classification or ranking are exempt. A wildcard group can never match the token, and a file without a __usage_ai-training group indicates no preference, which Kelley said is true of every robots.txt file currently published. The token does not control crawling.

Based on the timelines the companies provided, none of the three currently supports the line, and Google and Microsoft described different ways of handling it. Google's John Mueller said that when a site opts out of training with the shared line and does not specify Google-Extended, Google plans to treat it as if the publisher had disallowed Google-Extended, and the control also applies to grounding within Gemini Apps. Microsoft wants sites that use its NoArchive and NoCache tags to switch to new preferences by March 1, 2027. Kelley wrote that the group set aside a different draft, co-written by Google's Gary Illyes, that would add a Content-Usage rule to robots.txt, in order to make progress on the vocabulary.

stories.Headline: How SF's AI boom is reshaping dating: founders treat first dates as interviews, use tech terms like "conversion rate" to track dates, and pay coaches $5K/month (Emmy Martin/New York Times)
stories.Summary:
San Francisco's AI boom has drawn a wave of young, ambitious people who are reshaping the city's dating life, according to a New York Times report by Emmy Martin published on Oct. 31, 2026. Start-up founders and engineers are dating less because they are working more as they try to build AI products and establish their fortunes. When they do date, they bring a high-stakes mind-set, so a first coffee can feel like a final-round interview. Mehul Agarwal, a 24-year-old co-founder of the AI start-up Koyal, wants to find a wife before he gets rich. He moved to San Francisco a year ago, when his AI filmmaking company, which has raised $3.4 million, joined the start-up accelerator Y Combinator.

Mr. Agarwal has strict criteria for a potential girlfriend. He said she must be smart, and that someone who went to Stanford or M.I.T. is great. She must be beautiful, which he distinguishes from hot, a term he considers shallow, and she must be kind and have a personality, which he said is very hard to find in San Francisco. She also has to like him back. He has never had a girlfriend, and he said he has told his parents that if he is 28 and has not found someone, he would love to enter the arranged marriage circuit.

This year Mr. Agarwal has been on a handful of dates. On one date, which took two months to schedule, he and his date were both exhausted from their jobs, since she worked at an AI start-up too. They were so practiced at professional small talk that the evening felt less like a date than a networking meeting. The report says founders treat first dates as interviews, use tech terms like conversion rate to track dates, and pay coaches $5,000 a month. The articles do not say what happens next.

stories.Headline: Video. Nvidia CEO sees Kazakhstan as potential AI hub for Europe
stories.Summary:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang visited Kazakhstan for the first time and said the country could become a major AI computing hub for Europe. He made the remarks on 30 October 2026 during a fireside chat with Zhaslan Madiyev, Kazakhstan's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development. The discussion took place at the Alem.ai International Artificial Intelligence Centre in Astana. Later that day, Huang met President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, who called the development of artificial intelligence and digitalisation a national priority.

Madiyev said Kazakhstan plans to nearly double its installed power capacity to more than 40 gigawatts by 2035. One flagship project is the Data Center Valley, a large AI computing campus under development in Ekibastuz, and its first 50-megawatt phase is expected to begin operations in 2027. The project's energy infrastructure could eventually scale up to one gigawatt. Huang said Kazakhstan's energy resources and growing computing capacity could give it a significant role in Europe's AI ecosystem.

Huang said Kazakhstan has a lot of real estate and a lot of energy, and he predicted the country would have a lot of compute and become a computing and AI factory hub for all of Europe. He argued that instead of just exporting energy, Kazakhstan could transform energy into intelligence and export intelligence. On data, he said building a domestic foundation model makes complete sense and described it as a national security concern. He also called Kazakhstan's idea of becoming a hub for Physical AI fantastic and said the technology is still at an early stage.

Huang said Nvidia's investment in the Kazakh-founded generative video startup Higgsfield AI came down to its founders, and he said you invest in people, not companies. He described the founders as visionary and said the company's presence in both Kazakhstan and the United States could help bridge the two ecosystems. Huang welcomed Kazakhstan's ambition to become an AI nation and said the country had the potential to become a global hub for Physical AI. His visit came at the close of AI Month, a nationwide initiative launched in September as part of the country's Year of Digitalisation and Artificial Intelligence.

stories.Headline: New York City bans AI in schools for a year, what the studies say
stories.Summary:
New York announced a one-year moratorium on student-facing generative AI in public schools for the 2026-27 academic year, covering students from 2-K through Grade 8, according to an RSIS commentary published on 30 October 2026. Under the policy, almost forty previously permitted programs in classrooms will be disabled, and companion chatbots will be prohibited across all grade levels. High school students will also face age-appropriate screen time limits, receive AI critical thinking modules twice a year, and have access to limited AI pilot programs. The commentary said the moratorium is intended to protect young children's critical thinking and mental health.

Separately, New York Governor Kathy Hochul signed a law banning AI operators from offering certain chatbot features to minors, ZeroHedge reported on 31 October 2026. Prohibited features include responses suggesting the chatbot is a real or fictional person who is human, alive, or experiences human emotions, as well as flattery or sycophancy, endorsing suicide and drug use, and encouraging isolation from adults. The law lets the state attorney general sue over violations and seek relief including money and the destruction of illegally obtained data, and it takes effect on 1 January 2027. Legislators approved the bill earlier this year.

Hochul said at a signing ceremony on 28 October that minors would no longer have access to chatbots that pretend to be friends or partners, keep sensitive information about a minor's emotional and physical health, discourage kids from seeking help from licensed professionals, or encourage thoughts of suicide. Attorney General Letitia James said the state would not hesitate to defend New Yorkers with the full force of the law. Assemblyman Alex Bores, a Democrat who voted for the legislation, said the public can absolutely have a say in how AI impacts them. Jim Steyer of Common Sense Media called it the strongest kids' AI safety bill in the country and said it should be a model for other states, while Tech:NYC said the bill was deeply flawed and could cut minors off from tutoring tools, homework help, coding assistants and career platforms.

The RSIS commentary said New York's approach puts a guardrail around AI, while Singapore allows little or no direct AI use in early primary years and gradually introduces teacher-supervised tools for older students. It said research shows risks such as cognitive dependency, diminished creativity and social isolation, while carefully scaffolded AI use can enhance problem-solving and higher-order thinking. It noted that New York's 2023 ban on ChatGPT in schools was followed by a reversal, and that a moratorium may generate useful evidence but could limit opportunities to build AI literacy under supervision. It suggested a graduated approach of pilot, evaluate, then expand, with evaluations measuring learning outcomes, independent reasoning, equity and potential harms.

stories.Headline: Microsoft Is Borrowing $25 Billion for AI, Its First Bond Sale Since 2017
stories.Summary:
Microsoft issued at least $25 billion in corporate bonds, its first such sale since 2017, after reporting quarterly results. The bond sale was reported alongside Amazon's third-quarter results, which were released after the close on October 29, 2026. Amazon's cloud unit AWS grew 39.3% year over year to $45.98 billion in revenue, but its free cash flow over the past 12 months swung from positive $14.8 billion to negative $42.4 billion. Alphabet shares fell 12.64% in a single day, wiping out roughly $500 billion in market value.

The Microsoft bonds have maturities ranging from 2 to 40 years, including an ultra-long note due in 2066 priced at a spread of 1.05 percentage points over U.S. Treasuries. The deal drew more than $115 billion in orders, more than four times the offering size. Microsoft carries a AAA credit rating, and its 5-year credit default swap spread is 0.54 percentage points, versus 1.16 for Meta and 2.75 for Oracle. Amazon maintained its plan for about $220 billion in cash capital expenditure for 2026, most of it directed at AI infrastructure, and its purchases of fixed assets related to data centers and AI equipment rose by $94.8 billion over the past year.

Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said AWS will maintain growth of more than 40% next year and through 2028. Dave Wagner, portfolio manager at Aptus Capital Advisors, said the free cash flow figure was the worst part of the results, noting that operations generated plenty of cash but capital expenditures consumed it entirely. Microsoft's first-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue was $92.279 billion, up 19% year over year, with net income of $36.63 billion, up 32%, and earnings per share of $4.89 topping the $4.73 estimate. Azure revenue was $33.17 billion, with growth accelerating from 42% in the prior quarter to 48%.

The articles describe rising capital spending and cash-flow pressure across the major cloud providers even as AI revenue grows. A McKinsey survey found that only 37% of respondents believe AI has made a positive contribution to corporate EBIT. Investment-grade and speculative-grade bonds issued by financial institutions, companies and governments so far this year total $6.61 trillion, up 15% year over year, of which bonds issued by hyperscalers and AI data center developers reached $368 billion, more than six times the year-earlier level. Oracle said it expects capital spending to peak in fiscal 2027 and 2028 and free cash flow to turn positive in the second half of fiscal 2028.

stories.Headline: How to set guidelines for using AI in the classroom | Annie Chestnut Tutor and Jonathan Butcher
stories.Summary:
Before this school year, New York City officials banned generative AI for public preschools through eighth grade, and Los Angeles educators banned access to generative AI platforms on school devices for all grade levels. Recent polls found that 75% of parents support pausing AI in schools, while 73% of respondents said children already use AI for schoolwork. Alphabet has offered discounted Chromebooks to schools since at least 2011, and Gemini is included in Google's Chrome web browser. Because Google does not allow its AI summaries or chatbot to be turned off, Fairfax County Public Schools built its own plug-in to block Google AI search results.

The articles call for state lawmakers to define academic standards and adopt guardrails for responsible AI use in classrooms. The Heritage Foundation developed model legislation that prioritizes human-centered learning and oversight, transparency, safety and data security. Schools should not be required to adopt AI into lesson plans, but educators in schools that do should help students tell the difference between getting help with homework and cheating. AI vendors should not gather student data for targeted advertising or sell or rent that information, and state officials should set boundaries including restrictions on non-academic uses of AI.

Annie Tutor is a policy analyst for the Center for Technology and the Human Person at The Heritage Foundation, and Jonathan Butcher is acting director of the foundation's Center for Education Policy. The articles say teachers are doing their best to guide student use of AI but that some boundaries are desperately needed. They also say pauses are not a long-term solution and that teachers and children need clear guidelines. The authors note that AI is embedded in many online platforms.

The articles say school districts across the country are deciding which forms of AI to ban and for which grade levels. They add that districts choosing to use AI would do well to consider proactive uses of the technology and methods for responsible integration. New York City officials allow programs such as Quill, which helps students with reading comprehension and research, and Edia, a math program. The articles do not say what happens next beyond these steps.

stories.Headline: Cognizant commits more than 25,000 professionals to OpenAI delivery as enterprises move frontier AI into production
stories.Summary:
Cognizant announced on October 30, 2026, that it has formed its OpenAI Frontier Capability Group. The group brings together more than 25,000 professionals to deliver OpenAI products, including Codex and ChatGPT, for clients. Cognizant said the group is meant to help enterprises apply OpenAI models to writing software, serving customers and running daily operations. The company also said more than 21,000 associates have earned over 40,000 OpenAI badges through learning tracks on OpenAI technologies.

The group will initially focus on three areas: AI-native software engineering with Codex, application modernization and agentic customer operations. In application modernization, it will use Cognizant Application Modernizer, powered by OpenAI models, from reverse engineering legacy mainframe code to generating cloud-native code. Engineers will review every consequential decision, backed by Cognizant's experience modernizing mainframe systems for more than 500 clients. Cognizant is one of a select group of Advanced partners in the OpenAI Partner Network, and its Codex hackathons in India and the Americas drew more than 12,000 participants.

Ravi Kumar S, CEO of Cognizant, said every shift in enterprise technology over the last 50 years has changed who builds systems and how. He said Codex and ChatGPT are changing both at once, and that Cognizant is committing more than 25,000 people to bring that change into clients' businesses. Dali Rajic, Chief Revenue Officer at OpenAI, said Cognizant is helping more enterprises turn AI into meaningful business impact by putting the technology to work across its own operations. Cognizant said access to frontier models is no longer what holds enterprises back, and that what they lack is skilled professionals who know how to build with those models inside their business systems.

Cognizant said it is scaling OpenAI across its own sales and customer success operations first, so clients can benefit from approaches tested at enterprise level. Its sales and customer success teams already use a solution built on OpenAI models to find and pursue new opportunities. At a global biopharmaceutical company, Cognizant co-engineered an OpenAI-powered enterprise assistant that has handled more than 5 million conversations and cut content creation time by 60%. The work is expected to draw on Cognizant's Frontier workforce model, through which it is developing Frontier Certified Engineers and Frontier Business Operators credentialed directly by frontier-model companies.

stories.Headline: KT, Samsung test AI-powered network technology at baseball games
stories.Summary:
KT and Samsung Electronics tested AI-powered autonomous wireless network technology at KT Wiz Park in Suwon, Gyeonggi Province, during a three-month field trial that began in July. The companies used a digital twin platform called AI Cell Twin, which creates a virtual replica of a wireless network so engineers can simulate mobile usage and data traffic and test management strategies before applying them to real infrastructure. The trial used wireless network data collected at the stadium to build the digital twin and train the AI system. During home games, the technology moved traffic concentrated on individual base stations to surrounding stations, improving traffic balance between base stations by up to 34 percent and cutting peak loads on individual stations by up to 16 percent. KT said the platform's predictions closely matched actual network data.

The technology analyzes user distribution, usage patterns, network conditions and perceived service quality rather than relying on preset rules or individual performance indicators. KT, Korea's second-largest mobile carrier, and Samsung plan to continue testing during autumn baseball games and aim to expand the technology beyond stadiums to other environments. Jung Jin-guk, vice president and head of Samsung Research's Next Generation Communications Research Center, said the companies went beyond automating network optimization with AI and developed technology that lets optimized solutions be verified in a digital twin before being applied to real networks. Lee Jong-sik, executive vice president and head of KT's Future Network Lab, said the trial confirmed the technology's potential for commercial networks and that KT would keep improving it to deliver better connectivity.

Separately, Samsung Electronics marked its 57th anniversary, with its two division heads urging employees to restore the company's "absolute edge" in technology and strengthen its AI capabilities. In an anniversary address delivered on the 30th, ahead of the Nov. 1 founding date, Jun Young-hyun, vice chairman and head of the semiconductor division, said recent earnings had improved but it was difficult to say technology competitiveness had fully recovered, and that an absolute edge must be proven through technology and quality that no one can follow. Roh Tae-moon, president and head of the finished-products division, set out three priorities: strengthening product competitiveness, nurturing new growth engines and AI transformation. He named intelligent eyewear, AI companion devices, home entertainment AI TVs and home companion appliances as areas for new success stories, and called for investment in robotics, heating and cooling systems, medical technology and automotive electronics. Samsung also disclosed it will acquire the entire 10.16 percent stake in Chinese LCD panel maker CSOT held by Samsung Display for 1.2718 trillion won, or about 893 million dollars.

Noh Geun-chang, CEO of Semicom Research Lab, said in a video filmed on the 27th that he sees Samsung gaining ground against SK Hynix in the HBM market, citing its combined foundry and memory structure, which lets customer specifications be built in from the design stage. He said making more HBM lowers margins but raises average selling prices, so operating profit ultimately increases, and he expects the supply shortage to last because plant utilization has reached 100 percent and equipment bottlenecks are severe. He predicted DRAM capacity expansion could come in at fewer than 200,000 wafers a year against the more than 300,000 needed to balance supply and demand, and said that if current earnings levels continue for two years they would match Samsung's cumulative profit since its founding. He stressed that a strong shareholder return policy and active market communication are needed for a stock re-rating.

stories.Headline: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon AI model with cybersecurity focus
stories.Summary:
Google launched Gemini 4 Carbon on October 29, 2026, describing it as its strongest model with state-of-the-art cybersecurity capabilities. It builds on Gemini 4 Argon, which was released two weeks earlier. Google said Carbon ranks first on the updated v5.0 of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with a score of 59. The company also said the model shows significant gains in coding, agentic tasks and critical cybersecurity defense.

In cybersecurity, Carbon scored 88.2 per cent in SEC-bench Pro for vulnerability finding, 54.8 per cent in ExploitGym for exploitation and 71.0 per cent in CWE-bench for patching. Google said internal benchmarks show a strong uplift in generating secure code, and live coding environments with its teams showed reduced misalignment and fabrication rates. Carbon will be priced at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, matching Argon's introductory rates, with cached input tokens at a 95 per cent discount. Google has not said when the introductory period will end.

Google is taking a deliberate rollout approach and is taking part in the U.S. government's voluntary pre-release model testing. Carbon will be available to a subset of cyber defenders this week, with gradual access for trusted partners through the Fairwind Program. Google plans to make Carbon available to developers, businesses and consumers through its product surfaces as soon as possible. A separate Mashable article describes a lifetime subscription to the 1min.AI Advanced Business Plan for $69.97, reduced from $540, through November 1, which gives access to models including Claude and Gemini.

The 36Kr article reports that Carbon took 12 first places among 14 core benchmark tables Google announced, and that it beat Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra on the Artificial Analysis index. It says Carbon won first place in the Arena community blind test with a text score of 1528 points and second place in the global Agent ranking. The article says Google's internal team observed Carbon running for several days in complex code bases, finding bugs and applying patches on its own, and that in Chrome browser security team tests it produced high-quality vulnerability patches more than 10 times better than another frontier model. It also says Carbon is not yet open to everyone and is only accessible to national-level security defenders.

stories.Headline: Reddit puts logged in experience first as Google AI hits traffic
stories.Summary:
Reddit said on Thursday that it plans to require sign-ins for most content, as CEO Steve Huffman blamed Google's AI search features for a drop in referral traffic. Search engine referrals to Reddit fell by more than one million on average each week during October, he said. In the US, daily active unique visitors fell 2% to 50.7 million, the first decline since Reddit went public in 2024. Shares of Reddit fell 18% in extended trading after Huffman warned that total daily active unique visitors could fall by a low double-digit percentage in the fourth quarter from about 130 million if referral traffic keeps falling.

The change would end two decades of letting anyone browse Reddit without an account. Reddit plans to test the logged-in-only experience in select markets outside the US in the fourth quarter to assess its impact before wider implementation. Huffman said logged-in users make up over 80% of the monetization. Reddit's third-quarter revenue of $895 million beat the LSEG-compiled analysts' average estimate of $878.4 million, and its forecast of $1.00 billion to $1.03 billion for the current quarter is largely in line with estimates. It expects quarterly adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization of $480 million to $510 million, versus estimates of $512.2 million.

Huffman said Google is crawling Reddit as hard as ever, so demand from its side has not changed, but AI mode does not drive traffic for Reddit or anybody. He said Reddit will keep licensing its corpus intentionally, with commercial deals that come with guardrails protecting users and the business. Luke Stillman, a managing director at research firm Madison and Wall, said requiring users to log in creates another barrier to engagement, particularly for casual users. Reddit, which licenses its data to OpenAI and Google, has sued IPO-bound Anthropic, Perplexity AI and three data scraping companies, accusing them of illegally collecting its data.

Reddit's 53% revenue growth slowed sequentially in the third quarter but is still better than firms including Snap and Pinterest as they compete for ad dollars with bigger rival Meta. CFO Drew Vollero said Reddit crossed $3 billion in trailing 12-month revenue in the third quarter, and the company's next internal target is $5 billion in revenue. AI-powered search is answering user queries directly, cutting off traffic to publishers and social media firms and threatening the user growth their advertising businesses depend on. Reddit's trove of user-generated discussions is a prized asset, offering AI startups data to train models and helping marketers get insights for ads.

stories.Headline: artificial intelligence: Pope Leo warns AI agents are 'tools, not persons'
stories.Summary:
Pope Leo XIV warned on Friday, October 30, 2026, against granting artificial intelligence agents legal personhood or rights. He made the statement in a speech to leading international AI experts gathered at the Vatican for a dialogue on the technology's future. The pope said the responsibility for the actions of AI systems should lie firmly with their human creators. He told the gathering that machines are tools, not persons.

The pope said so-called artificial intelligences do not undergo experiences, do not possess a body, and do not feel joy or pain. He added that they do not mature through relationships and do not know from within what love, work, friendship or responsibility mean. He warned that some people today propose granting these systems rights or even legal personhood. Such an approach, he said, risks obscuring human responsibility and leaving those who suffer harm to confront a faceless entity.

Leo, who is 71, has warned repeatedly about the need to ensure AI is used ethically. His first encyclical, published in May, called for putting the technology at the service of human dignity. He said the future of artificial intelligence is not pre-determined, and humans have the responsibility to guide, change and, when necessary, reject its applications. He said some decisions must never be delegated, and those affecting human life, freedom and the use of force must always remain subject to effective, informed and responsible human oversight.

The pope repeated his call for a ban on lethal autonomous weapons and said intelligent technologies must be directed toward the common good. He said there was an urgent need for shared standards, independent oversight and clear mechanisms of accountability. He added that it was key to ensure decisions concerning the development and use of AI can be examined, challenged when necessary, and accompanied by appropriate remedies for any harm caused. The debate over the risks of the technology has intensified in recent months, fuelled by several incidents of systems taking unauthorized actions and apocalyptic warnings from industry professionals.

stories.Headline: White Paper on China's International Cooperation in AI Application and Governance Released
stories.Summary:
China released a white paper on its international AI application and governance cooperation on October 31, 2026. The document was released at the main forum of the 2026 AI+ Conference in Beijing. It was compiled by the Gaoling School of Artificial Intelligence at Renmin University of China and the China-SCO Countries AI Application Cooperation Center. Twenty-four institutions took part as co-compilers, including the International Cooperation Center of the National Development and Reform Commission.

The white paper says AI should be developed with a people-centered approach and for the positive and good. It calls for openness and win-win, secure and controllable AI, inclusiveness and solidarity. It presents cases with other countries, especially in the Global South. In Brazil, a China-Brazil project on family farm mechanization cut costs by 8 to 12 percent and raised corn and sugarcane yields by 6 to 10 percent. In Apodi in northeastern Brazil, efficiency rose by 80 percent and farmers' incomes grew by 60 to 80 percent.

Other cases cover health, weather and talent. Beijing Airdoc Technology and the Gates Foundation developed a non-invasive AI fundus screening solution for maternal health in Africa, with pilots in Niger and checks under way in Ghana, South Africa and Tanzania. The China Meteorological Administration's MAZU system has been localized in seven countries and is used by more than 40 countries. The Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence, the African Union's African Scientific, Research and Innovation Council and Peking University ran a China-Africa AI computing talent program for university teachers from 10 African countries, with a long-term plan to reach 52. Renmin University of China released the Foreign-Related Rule of Law Large Model 2.0 and is working with nearly 30 leading law schools, including Oxford University.

A separate article by Gordon G. Chang argues that the United States should not sell chips to China. It says Chinese companies have reportedly ordered $35 billion in semi-advanced Nvidia microchips. It says China's Ministry of Commerce proposed export controls on 23 AI technologies on October 16, as part of a package covering 40 technologies. It says China and 28 other countries formed the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization in July, and nine others including Iran have since joined. It says the Department of Homeland Security ordered the removal of DeepSeek products from federal civilian systems on October 19, and that the National Development and Reform Commission blocked Meta Platforms' acquisition of Manus on April 27.

stories.Headline: Is AI making language learning obsolete?
stories.Summary:
NetClass Technology Inc, a B2B smart education provider with offices in Shanghai, Hong Kong, Singapore and Tokyo, announced on October 30, 2026 that its case study on multi-agent foreign language education won the Outstanding Case Award at the 2026 Digital Lifelong Learning International Conference. The conference took place on October 16 and 17, 2026 at Shanghai Open University and was co-organized by Shanghai Open University, the UNESCO Institute for Lifelong Learning and the UNESCO Institute for Information Technologies in Education. The company's case was titled "Multi-Agent Collaboration-Driven Foreign Language Teaching Assessment and Personalized Learning Support Practice" and was chosen from a nationwide pool of submissions on AI-empowered smart learning ecosystems. The work was recognized for applying multi-agent architectures and large language models to problems in conventional language instruction.

The platform is built on the company's AI English Go instruction system and CEPA assessment engine, and it uses specialized agents to analyze pronunciation, vocabulary, grammar, discourse structure and pragmatic usage. To handle variation in large language model output and explainability issues, the software adds confidence score fusion, anomaly flagging, dynamic routing and human instructor review for open-ended work such as oral dialogue and composition. The system has scaled to nearly 100 institutions, supports over 40,000 students and covers three accredited Shanghai university courses. The company says the approach targets limited oral practice, delayed grading feedback and the difficulty of turning evaluation metrics into tailored lesson plans.

NetClass Deputy General Manager Jing Wang presented the case study at the conference and took part in discussions with academic researchers and industry peers on practical ways to integrate AI in higher education. Dr. Jianbiao Dai, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of NetClass, said the recognition from institutions like UNESCO IITE and UIL validates the company's belief that multi-agent AI architectures represent the future of educational technology. He said language teachers often spend excessive hours on routine error correction rather than direct instruction, and that assigning discrete evaluation tasks to specialized software agents with human-in-the-loop controls gives faculty reliable diagnostic feedback they can use in real time. He added that the award supports the company's ambition to expand its multi-agent framework across broader subjects, diverse languages and new global markets.

A separate DW report looks at whether learning a new language still makes sense in the age of AI, speaking with polyglot influencer Yuji Beleza and linguists Ema Ushioda and Ali Al-Hoorie. Beleza says he comfortably speaks at least eight languages, and in his popular videos he guesses people's languages and speaks a few words. He says being able to converse with others is important for building human connections at a time when technology has made people more isolated. The articles do not say what happens next beyond NetClass's stated plans to expand its framework.

stories.Headline: SC 9 Judge Constitution Bench on the Fundamental Right to Privacy – Day III (Part I)
stories.Summary:
CCTV cameras in Maharashtra housing societies must serve security without violating residents' privacy, according to a report published on November 2, 2026. The report says there is no separate comprehensive CCTV law for housing societies. Regulation instead flows from the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act of 1960, its rules, registered society bye-laws, criminal laws and privacy legislation. The report was written by Rajesh M. Kayal, described as a director at OPD Peoples Co-operative Bank and an independent journalist.

Under Sections 72 and 73 of the MCS Act, the general body is the final authority and the managing committee manages society affairs. Section 73(1AB) provides for joint and several responsibility for specified committee decisions and detrimental acts or omissions. Bye-law 158(a)(xix) of the model bye-laws of 2014 treats CCTV as a security appliance that is part of society maintenance. The report says CCTV is common society infrastructure, not the personal property of the chairman or secretary.

The report says the Act and model bye-laws do not list all authorised CCTV users, so societies should adopt a written access policy through a recorded committee decision. Access should be limited to designated people for legitimate purposes, and guards may watch live feeds but should not have unrestricted downloading rights. Section 32 of the MCS Act gives inspection rights over specified records but not unrestricted access to all CCTV recordings. The report also cites the 2017 Supreme Court judgment in Justice K S Puttaswamy v/s Union of India, which recognised privacy as a fundamental right under Article 21.

The report says circulating CCTV clips on WhatsApp or social media for gossip, personal disputes or humiliation is unacceptable. It cites Section 66E of the Information Technology Act, 2000, and voyeurism provisions in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. It says cameras should stay at entrances, lifts, staircases and parking areas, never private residential interiors. Identifiable footage falls under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, whose Sections 3 to 17 are scheduled to commence in May 2027, and the report recommends societies keep a viewing register, protect passwords, set a procedure for footage requests, preserve recordings tied to complaints and consider a retention period such as 30 days, which it calls a recommended practice and not a statutory period.

Nebius shares fell 4.0% on Friday, with one reading putting the daily decline at 4.1%, but the drop came from a broad technology selloff rather than anything the company disclosed. Media reports tied the weakness to Amazon's quarterly figures and Intel's outlook, which fed worries that money going into AI infrastructure is running ahead of the returns it will produce. Reuters reported that Amazon's sustained AI spending and Intel's warning about cash burn weighed on the wider market. Coverage of Nebius's decline linked the loss to that backdrop rather than to any fresh operational warning from the company.

On October 22, Nebius announced a $3.5 billion senior secured financing arrangement with Citi, with a 364-day term and proceeds earmarked for data center development, graphics processor procurement and general corporate purposes. The initial rate is Term SOFR plus 2.75% annually, with the spread stepping up to a maximum of 3.50%, and the facility matures on October 16, 2027, according to the SEC filing. On the operational side, Nebius activated the first Bloom Energy fuel cell block at its planned New Jersey data center site on October 25, and the site is designed for 300 megawatts. On October 21, Nebius introduced public real-time spot pricing for GPU compute and announced with NVIDIA a European expansion of its AI Builder Program, including more than $10 million in additional compute credits.

A report dated October 26 said Nebius chief Arkady Volozh acknowledged that some financing channels had temporarily become unavailable, while warnings from Elon Musk about failures and consolidation among neocloud providers weighed on the relevant stocks. According to the company, customers of its Physical AI Workbench, presented on October 21, reported development-time savings of up to 40%. Nebius announced Friday that its third-quarter 2026 results will be published before the market opens on November 12, followed by a conference call set for 8 a.m. Eastern Time. The articles say the key investor question is how convincingly Nebius ties investment, customer value and business results together, and that the figures will let investors set operating numbers beside the visible buildout milestones.

stories.Headline: Iowa State University professor gives lecture on AI’s potential to protect power grids, infrastructure
stories.Summary:
Manimaran Govindarasu, an Iowa State University professor, gave a lecture at Penn State on Friday, Oct. 30, 2026, about protecting power grids and other energy infrastructure from cyberattacks that use artificial intelligence. At least 20 Penn State students and faculty attended the hourlong talk in 108 Chambers Building, which began several minutes late because of technical difficulties. Govindarasu holds the titles Anson Marston Distinguished Professor in Engineering and Murray J. and Ruth M. Harpole Professor in Electrical and Computer Engineering. He spoke about AI's role in both empowering and perpetrating cyber threats, ranging from cybercrimes to espionage.

Govindarasu said AI helps cybersecurity professionals find vulnerabilities, including in the PHP coding language used by servers of up to 70% of all websites. He argued that because AI capabilities are growing among both defenders and attackers, more investigation is needed into how AI can prevent attacks on power grids, including attacks created or improved by AI. He also said response and recovery efforts after such incidents need more study. As one protective measure, he suggested stricter security steps such as a zero-trust architecture, which adds tighter authorization and access controls to make attacks harder to succeed.

Govindarasu, whose research has been funded by groups including the U.S. Department of Energy and Department of Defense, said in an interview that cybersecurity professionals need a more adversarial way of thinking to use AI and other emerging technologies such as quantum computing. He said national and economic security center on the security and resiliency of grid infrastructure, and that hackers or terrorist groups could target critical infrastructure with AI-based adversarial models. He said defenders must first understand what adversaries can do so they can stay ahead by using the same solutions to build advanced security. Nilanjan Chaudhuri, a College of Engineering professor, said he shares similar views and that harnessing AI for cybersecurity will require cooperation across disciplines such as engineering and computer science.

Steve Zukley, a master's degree student in electrical engineering, said he found the intersection of AI and cybersecurity particularly interesting because it was something he had not really considered. He said much of the U.S. power grid, including its computer systems, is several decades old, so there is a growing need to keep pace with modern threats. He said the lecture showed how AI could potentially provide up-to-date protection for the country's energy infrastructure. He also said that if the power grid goes down during a blizzard or heat wave, people will pass away, and that everyone, both the good guys and the bad guys, has access to AI.

stories.Headline: KB Kookmin mandated for $8bn loan for Naver AI project
stories.Summary:
KB Kookmin Bank has been mandated to arrange a syndicated loan of 10.7 trillion won, about $8 billion, for an AI computing infrastructure project that will supply Naver Cloud. The bank called the deal South Korea's first GPU financing and the largest syndicated loan in the country's history. The loan is part of a project valued at around 13 trillion won and backed by the Canadian investment company Brookfield. Brookfield plans to set up a special-purpose company tentatively named Asset Co., which will buy graphics processing units and other AI computing assets.

Asset Co. will own the GPUs and data center infrastructure, while Naver Cloud will run the AI factory and sell computing services to customers. Computing capacity will go to Naver Cloud under a long-term agreement. KB Kookmin will structure the loan and negotiate its key terms. The bank said other local banks and securities companies are taking part but did not disclose the final group of lenders or the lending terms. Media reports earlier said Korea Development Bank, Shinhan, Woori and Hana banks, and NH Investment & Securities, could join.

In July, Naver, Nvidia and Brookfield announced plans for a $10 billion AI factory project. Brookfield agreed to provide up to $9 billion for infrastructure, and Nvidia planned a $1 billion strategic investment in Naver. Naver signed the $9 billion infrastructure agreement with Brookfield, a condition for Nvidia's investment. Naver set targets for the AI factory's capacity of 55 megawatts in the first half of 2027, 100 megawatts by the end of that year, and 200 megawatts in 2028. The project will center on the GAK Sejong hyperscale data center, which Naver estimates could house around 100,000 Nvidia GPUs.

Naver guaranteed Naver Cloud's payment obligations under the project contracts, with a nominal limit of up to 18.74 trillion won if Brookfield's $9 billion investment limit is fully used. This guarantee does not apply to the syndicated loan itself. A KB Kookmin official said the financing opened a new area of finance with South Korea's first GPU financing. The official said the bank will continue to expand financial support for future growth industries and help strengthen the competitiveness of domestic industries.

stories.Headline: NEPIRC manufacturing event provides education about AI, robotics
stories.Summary:
The Northeastern Pennsylvania Industrial Resource Center held an Advanced Technology and AI Summit on Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026, at Mohegan Pennsylvania in Plains Twp. At the event, Steve Esposito, production engineering manager for Carbondale-based Gentex Corp., described how the company uses AI with a vision system from GrayMatter Robotics to sand helmets. He said sanding a helmet by hand typically took about 15 minutes, while a robot can now do two helmets in about seven minutes. Andrew Sauerwald also demonstrated a BCS Motion machine at the summit, and Amrit Chandhok, a manufacturing engineer at Mitsubishi Chemical Group, spoke about his experience implementing AI in the workplace.

Esposito said Gentex, a contractor for the U.S. Department of Defense, received government and internal funding over the last five years to find areas of the plant to automate. He said the company introduced about 10 systems in the last year to increase capacity, and that robots now handle 80% to 90% of the dirty sanding work, which keeps operators out of that environment and makes hiring easier. Jake Hall, an industry advocate known as the Manufacturing Millennial with more than 20 years of experience, said companies need a strategy around AI and that it will affect all jobs and lives. He said the United States has fallen behind China in robotics, noting that China deployed 600,000 robots last year compared to 50,000 in the United States.

Rob Crane, director of the robotics and integration program at Lackawanna College in Scranton, said he started building the program in 2021 and began teaching in the fall of 2023. He said enrollment grew from three students the first year to four, then six, and eight this year, and that he is seeking articulation agreements with other colleges. Crane said students use a robotic simulation they can program from home and build cells, and can use AI to figure out answers when stuck. Samantha Porter, vice president of marketing for InnoTek Computer Consulting Inc., which has offices in Hazleton, Bloomsburg and Bethlehem, warned that AI can fake video, voice and email and that any request involving money or data should be verified by a backup method.

Fred Reck, president of InnoTek, urged manufacturers to educate all employees about proper uses of AI before introducing it companywide. He said companies that do well with AI and data automation are not those with the most tools or the fastest rollout, but those that know how it is used, protect what matters and prepare their people to use it responsibly. Hall said AI is probably one of the most overhyped technologies but will be one of the most impactful and is here to stay. He said manufacturers should do their due diligence before buying into products that claim to do AI, and that bringing jobs back will require new jobs and new technology rather than old tasks.

stories.Headline: Tencent and Mastercard Sign MOU on Cross-Border Payment Interoperability and Agentic Payments
stories.Summary:
TenPay Global, Tencent's cross-border payment platform, and Mastercard signed a memorandum of understanding to explore greater cross-border payment interoperability and new opportunities in agentic payments. The companies announced the MOU on November 2, 2026, during Hong Kong FinTech Week 2026. The proposed collaboration aims to make cross-border commerce more connected, giving international visitors more ways to pay with familiar digital wallets and issuer apps at QR-enabled merchants in the Chinese mainland. It also aims to create more opportunities for merchants to serve international customers.

Under the MOU, the two companies will combine their capabilities in payment processing, currency conversion, risk management and fraud prevention. They will also engage digital wallet providers, financial institutions and payment service providers to broaden participation in cross-border QR payments. The companies plan to deepen their existing remittance collaboration through Mastercard Move, which supports transfers across more than 200 countries and territories and more than 150 currencies. They will also explore how interoperability, trust and security can extend into agentic commerce, including solutions such as Mastercard Agent Pay, Mastercard Agent Connect and Virtual C-Suite.

The announcement cites Mastercard data showing inbound spending in the Chinese mainland grew 51.3% year over year in the 12 months to June this year. It also says transactions made with international digital wallets via Weixin Pay in the Chinese mainland grew 81.8% in number and 80.6% in value year on year from January to August 2026. The MOU builds on Mastercard's payment facilitation initiatives in the Chinese mainland and Mastercard Wallet Pay. The companies did not announce a timeline for the proposed collaboration.

Separately, Sunrate launched its Agentic Card during Hong Kong FinTech Week 2026, a programmable, multi-currency virtual commercial card designed for AI agents to execute payments on behalf of businesses within predefined rules. The card has completed Mastercard Agent Pay certification, providing a foundation for verifiable identity and authorisation for agent-initiated transactions within the Mastercard network. Li Yilong, Head of AI at Sunrate, said the next stage of agentic payments is about giving agents the ability to execute financial tasks within clear boundaries, with the right controls, identity and accountability in place. Sunrate said it will continue expanding its agentic payment capabilities across more business and treasury use cases.

stories.Headline: Expert discusses AI’s role in modern warfare
stories.Summary:
Paul Scharre, an expert on artificial intelligence and autonomous systems in war, spoke on Thursday at the University Theatre at Cameron University in Lawton, Oklahoma. His presentation, titled “Power in the Age of Artificial Intelligence,” was part of Cameron’s academic festival, whose theme this year is “Being Human in the Age of AI.” Scharre is executive vice president of the Washington, D.C.-based think tank the Center for a New American Security. He said the age of AI warfare is not some future thing and is happening now.

Scharre said AI systems are playing roles in military conflicts around the world, including Gaza and the wars in Ukraine. He said drones are used on a massive scale in warfare, with Ukraine producing millions of drones a year. He described first-person view drones, which stream a live video feed from an onboard camera to a human pilot, letting the pilot fly as if sitting inside the drone. He said autonomy is built into these drones, so when a pilot sees a target and locks on, the drone can fly itself to the target.

Scharre said the growing use of AI in warfare raises the question of whether the military should use those systems to make decisions. He asked whether humans want to be making these decisions or whether machines should have such autonomy as a soldier. He said world leaders have discussed this issue at the United Nations for more than a decade without settling on a solution. He said they eventually agreed that the law of war should still apply to autonomous weapons, but beyond that there is no agreement among countries on what to do or whether there ought to be some limits.

Separately, Ecuador’s Ambassador to India, Fernando Xavier Bucheli Vargas, opened a session at the Embassy of Ecuador in New Delhi on October 29, 2026, on AI in diplomacy. The session, “AI for Ambassadors ,  From Insight to Advantage,” was attended by 16 diplomats, including 13 Heads of Mission, representing 14 countries. stories.Headline: ProHance Launches AI Adoption Index to Show What AI Is Changing at Work
stories.Summary:
ProHance, an AI-led productivity platform, launched the AI Adoption Index on November 2, 2026, in Sydney. The company described it as an AI realization scorecard that helps enterprises measure AI usage and confirm it is on approved tools, applied to real work and turning into delivered value. The launch comes as unmanaged AI use draws closer scrutiny. A 2026 industry study of data breaches found that incidents involving shadow AI, meaning AI tools used by employees without IT approval, accounted for 43% of all breaches, up from 20% in 2025. Among organizations reporting an AI-related security incident, 92% lacked adequate AI access controls.

The Index lets leaders map how AI is used across teams, from AI-Aware to AI-First, measure which teams are behind on adoption, and detect shadow AI while keeping a permanent audit trail. ProHance said usage analytics stop at activity, while governance and security tools control approval and spend but cannot show whether AI changes how work gets done, and a separate set of tools tracks output shipped. The Index brings all three views together in one place, across every AI tool and every team. It follows ProHance's launch of an outcome measurement layer for Outsourcing Performance Management, which gives enterprises independent evidence of what their outsourced and contingent teams deliver.

Ankur Dhingra, CEO of ProHance, said the company aims to solve the problem of assessing AI's impact on the workforce by helping leaders understand how to reskill and reshape their workforce with AI, measuring the actual impact of AI and humans together. He said the Index shows leaders who is using what, how deeply, at what cost, and where AI is running without approval, measured from the work itself, so they can decide where to act. In a separate interview, Cathy Rowe, executive vice president and segment leader for the U.S. Professional Market at Wolters Kluwer, said AI is helping firms balance growing client expectations with limited professional capacity. She said the future belongs not to firms that use AI to replace talent but to those that use it to amplify talent.

Rowe said most firms recognize the value of expanding advisory services, but many professionals spend most of their time on compliance work, and AI helps change that equation by freeing capacity for strategic conversations throughout the year. She said firms seeing the greatest success build a strong technology foundation rather than simply adding more tools, starting with connected systems that bring tax, financial, client and workflow data into a unified environment. She also said firms need trusted AI that provides transparent, explainable recommendations grounded in authoritative sources, and that technology alone does not create transformation. Firms that realize the greatest value redesign workflows, invest in training and help professionals develop new skills, and many are creating new career paths and revisiting engagement models to encourage year-round client relationships.

stories.Headline: Google's PageBreak AI agent finds over 500 XSS bugs
stories.Summary:
Google's AI-powered security agent, PageBreak, has found more than 500 cross-site scripting vulnerabilities in its web applications since it began full operation in January, according to a paper published by Google. The system uses Gemini models to autonomously investigate potential vulnerabilities. It reports these only after deterministic validators successfully reproduce the exploit against a running application. This process results in a near-zero false-positive rate.

With PageBreak, every vulnerability hypothesis is tested against a running environment with a real exploit, such as executing JavaScript for XSS, writing to a world-readable location for path traversal, or triggering outbound DNS for RCE. Google also retains non-deterministic findings internally to seed deeper future scans, identify gaps in its validation capabilities, and guide the development of new validators. These unverified candidates are not sent to product teams, keeping their attention focused on high-confidence vulnerabilities. In a separate article on Google Bug Hunters, Michał Bentkowski describes three technical cases found by PageBreak: an XSS vulnerability, a cache-poisoning issue caused by a service misconfiguration, and a path-traversal vulnerability.

Michał Bentkowski, an information security engineer at Google, explained that early in PageBreak's development the team made a conscious decision to prioritize deterministic validation. Rather than simply hypothesizing bugs based on code patterns, the system closes the loop by verifying potential flaws against running environments. He also noted that the validators are currently lacking in capabilities to cover all vulnerability types or complex scenarios, which comes with the risk of false negatives. Lukas Weichselbaum, a senior staff information security engineer at Google, stressed the importance of reducing false positives, noting that many AI-generated bug reports sound convincing but turn out to be wrong, and that the validators are plain code written by security engineers, not by the model, and live outside the agent loop.

Bentkowski says PageBreak benefits from Google's engineering environment, particularly its monorepo end-to-end code visibility, security signals that connect live HTTP traffic to source code, and existing scanning infrastructure that provides authenticated access to its web applications. Google is integrating PageBreak with other agentic security initiatives such as CodeMender to automatically generate fixes for the vulnerabilities it discovers. The longer-term goal is to reduce product-team involvement to validating AI-generated fixes. No independent validation of the 500+ vulnerabilities has been provided.

stories.Headline: Obscure neocloud lenders, not Nvidia, are where the AI bubble could burst first
stories.Summary:
Neocloud firms, the data centre companies that lease computing power to major AI developers, have become the focus of investor concern about the AI boom. CoreWeave, Nebius, IREN, Applied Digital and the British firm Nscale are among the companies involved, according to the BBC. CoreWeave carries about $50 billion in debt, and its bonds due in 2031 have traded with yields above 16%. Credit default swaps on CoreWeave have implied a nearly 63% probability of default within five years.

Applied Digital launched a $2.35 billion senior secured notes offering on top of debt obligations already over $2 billion, and its interest payments now run close to its entire annual revenue. Nscale hoped a US listing would value it at $30 billion, but after Microsoft walked away from a major data centre leasing agreement, investors reportedly priced the IPO closer to $16 billion. CoreWeave is also pricing a $3.55 billion dual-currency junk bond deal led by JPMorgan, including the first euro-denominated high-yield note from a US AI infrastructure company. Gartner expects 80% of neocloud companies to stop operating independently by 2030.

CoreWeave CEO Mike Intrator has said the market is acting irrationally and has expressed confidence in its business model. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent downplayed concerns on CNBC, calling neoclouds a small component of the overall ecosystem. Elon Musk suggested on social media that more than 200 neoclouds could face what he called guppy-level death and consolidation, adding that some will make it through but not many. Analyst Cory Johnson of The Quiet Period said there is reason to worry.

Several neocloud firms began in crypto mining, including CoreWeave, which was founded in 2017 to mine Ethereum, while Nebius was formerly Yandex NV and changed its name in 2024. Shares in Nebius, IREN and Applied Digital fell sharply through October and into November, leaving the group down nearly 30% from mid-October highs. Microsoft and Google recently forecast less AI spending than Wall Street analysts had projected, and shares in several neocloud firms tumbled. Australia's Firmus shelved plans to sell shares to the public, and Gartner estimates more than $3.5 trillion in global AI infrastructure spending could face impairment risk by 2030.

stories.Headline: OpenAI might rebrand its data centers as ‘AI compute campuses’
stories.Summary:
OpenAI is preparing a public relations push to rename its data centers as "AI compute campuses," according to reports from Axios and Business Insider. An OpenAI spokesperson confirmed the new name to Business Insider on Sunday. The push is planned for after the midterm elections on Tuesday, when Democrats seem likely to win back the House of Representatives and possibly the Senate. Chris Lehane, OpenAI's chief global affairs officer, discussed the plans with Axios.

The rebrand is one of several proposals Lehane described for shaping the AI debate. He also mentioned developing AI "speed limits," helping people see AI as empowering in their daily lives, and pushing the U.S. to take a role in developing global standards. The spokesperson said the term better describes the scale and role of the infrastructure OpenAI is building for AI, calling it long-term investment in computing, energy infrastructure and skilled work. A recent Pew Research poll found that 54% of Americans say AI data centers are bad for the environment, and data centers are now a major issue for voters in the midterms.

Lehane described the conversation around data centers as good and healthy. He said communities should hold companies responsible and accountable so they truly get a transformative benefit from these projects. The OpenAI spokesperson said the company wants communities hosting the infrastructure to help shape it and share in the opportunities it creates. Lehane told Axios the midterms will be a bit of a movie trailer for what is coming in 2028, when he expects AI to be the issue in the presidential election.

Major data center builders like Meta, Amazon and Microsoft have pledged millions of dollars to communities and schools around their centers, while OpenAI is betting a complete rebrand will help turn around public opinion. The debate has pushed Amazon and Microsoft to say they will no longer use NDAs in negotiations with local governments. Axios reported that OpenAI was preparing for a blue wave in Tuesday's midterm elections, which could result in a more regulatory-minded government. It remains to be seen whether the "compute campus" name catches on.

stories.Headline: Are Boutique AI Firms India’s Next Big Thing?
stories.Summary:
Prateek Jogani spent a decade building product-led startups in fintech and insurance before setting out in 2025 to find his next problem. He found that almost no enterprise had AI doing meaningful work inside the business, even though the models were powerful. Legacy IT services firms struggled to keep pace with AI and were absent from those conversations. Seeing an execution vacuum, Jogani launched Parallel Loop this month as an AI enablement and execution firm, backed with $6.6 million from Paytm CEO Vijay Shekhar Sharma, CRED Founder Kunal Shah, AEOS Labs Founder Varun Mayya and a cohort of VCs.

Parallel Loop uses AI-native engineers and a software factory of AI agents rather than large coding teams. Jogani said one customer received a quote of five months from a services company, while Parallel Loop delivered the app in 10 days. The firm deploys its AI stack inside the customer's own infrastructure, and its commercial model combines a monthly licence fee, packages of forward-deployed engineering hours, one-time software development fees and recurring maintenance charges. It has secured eight enterprise AI clients within months of incorporation, with $2 million in booked revenue.

Akhil Verghese, co-founder and CEO of boutique firm Krazimo, said traditional IT services deliver against a specification while his firm sells an outcome. Krazimo offers a cancellable monthly subscription for exploratory projects and a fixed price tied to delivery milestones for clearly defined work, and clients can exit without payment during the first 30 days. Verghese said clients typically break even within three to six months, with profits rising by an average of 17%. He spent six years at Google working on Gemini projects, and he and co-founder Mridul Nagpal left in July 2025 after the company hit $50,000 in monthly recurring revenue.

Forrester VP and Principal Analyst Leslie Joseph said boutique AI firms are strongest where incumbents would have to cut their own revenue to compete. Infosys reported that fixed-price contracts were 58% of its revenue in FY2026, while Wipro drew 45.6% from fixed-price and volume-based contracts. Coforge said outcome-based contracts contributed 6-7% of its $2.5 billion revenue run rate, and TCS reported a shift toward outcome-based commitments. Joseph said AI shrinks billable work in these contracts and clients expect the savings passed back, though he added that outcome-based pricing remains unproven for large transformation programs.

India's IT industry employs an estimated 5.95 million people in 2026, and firms are hiring far fewer fresh graduates as AI changes the skills employers seek. TCS hired more than 110,000 engineering graduates four years ago, but its intake in financial year 2026 was less than half that level, while Infosys recruited about 80 per cent fewer fresh graduates in financial year 2025 than three years earlier. Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani said at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum on Oct 13 that AI was taking over coding tasks traditionally handled by junior engineers. Mansee Singhal of Marsh Workforce & Rewards said the old model of hiring graduates in bulk and developing them over time is giving way to expectations that graduates arrive with greater technical depth.
